newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends near limit off on falling cash.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends near limit off on falling cash.

text.p: Start of the anticipated sharp decline in cash lumber prices kept speculative pressure on CME lumber futures and prices ended as much as near limit down.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $410 per tbf, down $20 from midweek and $22 under last Friday's level.

The break in cash markets had been anticipated for some time and reflects a combination of increased lumber supplies and stepped up inventory reduction which develops after Labor Day. Retailer demand for wood has been tailing off which should depress cash prices, especially ahead of the slow demand period into the fall and winter holidays, traders said.

Expectations point to cash spruce prices falling to the $370 to $375 per tbf area next week. Although futures are already at a sharp discount to current cash levels, they will remain under pressure until cash markets find a bottom, traders added.
Lumber closed $9.40 per tbf lower to unchanged with November off most at $340.90 and January off $4.00 at $349.70 per tbf.
